components.css: .ds-diagram{font-family:var(--font-sign, 'Roboto Condensed','Arial Narrow',sans-serif);margin:0;padding:10px 12px 8px;border:1px solid var(--color-rule,#e4e4e1);border-radius:6px;color:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-cap{font-weight:800;font-size:0.75rem;letter-spacing:0.06em;text-transform:uppercase}.ds-tracks{position:relative;padding-top:24px}.ds-guide{position:absolute;top:0;bottom:-2px;margin-left:24px;border-left:1px dashed rgb(29 29 27/.4);border-right:1px dashed rgb(29 29 27/.4);transition:left 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1),width 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)}.ds-pill{position:absolute;top:0;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);white-space:nowrap;padding:0 8px;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);color:#fff;font-weight:800;font-size:0.6875rem;line-height:1.125rem}.ds-lane{display:flex;align-items:center;height:20px;margin-top:4px}.ds-lane b{width:24px;flex:none;font-weight:800;font-size:0.8125rem}.ds-track{position:relative;flex:1;height:20px;background:linear-gradient(var(--color-rule,#e4e4e1),var(--color-rule,#e4e4e1)) center/100% 1px no-repeat}.ds-free{position:absolute;top:7px;height:6px;border-radius:9999px}.ds-busy{position:absolute;top:6px;height:8px;border-radius:2px;background-color:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);background-image:repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg,transparent 0 4px,rgb(255 255 255/.28) 4px 6px)}.ds-unknown{position:absolute;top:9px;height:2px;background-image:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,var(--color-mute,#555552) 0 5px,transparent 5px 10px)}.ds-plat{position:absolute;top:50%;height:14px;transform:translateY(-50%);box-sizing:border-box;border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);border-radius:9999px;background:#fff}.ds-station{margin:6px 0 0 24px;font-weight:800;font-size:0.75rem}

components.css: .ds-opt{font-family:var(--font-sign, 'Roboto Condensed','Arial Narrow',sans-serif);display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.75rem 1fr auto;gap:0 10px;padding:12px 4px 12px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule,#e4e4e1);background:var(--color-panel,#f4f4f2);color:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);cursor:pointer;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-ring{width:22px;height:22px;box-sizing:border-box;margin:2px 0 0 2px;border:5px solid var(--color-line-red,#e1251b);border-radius:9999px;background:#fff}.ds-day{display:block;font-weight:800;font-size:1.0625rem;line-height:1.25}.ds-span{font-weight:500;font-size:0.9375rem;color:var(--color-mute,#555552)}.ds-reasons{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:4px;margin-top:4px}.ds-reason{padding:1px 6px;border:1px solid var(--color-rule-strong,#bdbdb9);border-radius:3px;font-weight:700;font-size:0.6875rem}.ds-avs{display:flex;gap:3px;margin-top:6px}.ds-av{position:relative;display:grid;place-items:center;width:24px;height:24px;box-sizing:border-box;overflow:hidden;border:1.5px solid var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);border-radius:9999px;font-weight:800;font-size:0.6875rem}.ds-av-free{background:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);color:#fff}.ds-av-unknown{border-style:dashed;border-color:var(--color-mute,#555552);color:var(--color-mute,#555552)}.ds-av-busy::after{content:'';position:absolute;left:-2px;right:-2px;top:50%;height:1.5px;background:var(--color-ink,#1d1d1b);transform:rotate(-45deg)}.ds-count{text-align:right}.ds-count b{display:block;font-weight:800;font-size:1.25rem;line-height:1}.ds-count small{display:block;font-weight:500;font-size:0.6875rem;color:var(--color-mute,#555552)}.ds-best{display:inline-block;margin-top:8px;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:3px;background:var(--color-line-red,#e1251b);color:#fff;font-weight:800;font-size:0.6875rem}

narrative.overview:
Each friend is a metro line running across the day. Where every line runs free at once, a station appears, and that station is the option you confirm. The system refuses the category default of a days-by-people check table: availability is read as a transit diagram, not as a grid of ticks.

The material is enamel transit signage: a white ground, ink signs, Santiago Metro line colours, bold condensed type for every label and time. Everything is flat. Depth comes from ink panels and hairline rules, never from shadows or gradients. The density is phone-first and compact, one narrow column, because people answer in short bursts between classes or in transit. Light only, by design: signage is white enamel, and there is no dark theme.

State is carried by shape before colour. A free stretch is a solid coloured line, busy time is an ink hatched "out of service" segment, and a friend who hasn't answered is a grey dashed track that is never drawn as free. The same three shapes appear wherever availability appears, in the plan diagram and in the busy editor alike.
keyCharacteristics: White enamel ground, ink signage, one Santiago Metro line colour per person.
Free = solid line, busy = ink hatch, unknown = grey dashes; colour never carries state alone.
The station (the confirmable slot) is marked with dashed guides, an ink time pill and white platforms.
Roboto Condensed at heavy weights with tabular numerals for every time and count.
Flat: no shadows, no gradients; ink fills and hairline rules give structure.
One narrow phone column with a sticky action footer.

rules.name: The Line Belongs to a Person Rule
rules.body: Line colours are assigned one per person in join order: red, blue, yellow, green, purple, ink, then the cycle repeats. A line colour is never used as decoration or as a state signal; blue doubles as the action colour and red as the rank-one marker, both always paired with a shape or a word.

rules.name: The Yellow Outline Rule
rules.body: Yellow is always drawn with a 1px ink inset outline, because it fails 3:1 against white.

rules.name: The Shape Before Colour Rule
rules.body: Free, busy and unknown must stay distinguishable in greyscale: solid line, ink hatch, grey dashes. Unknown is never drawn as free.

rules.name: The Signage Weight Rule
rules.body: Labels, times and counts are set at 700–800; 400 is reserved for running text and captions that explain.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time and count uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs separation, give it an ink fill or a hairline, never a shadow.

dos: **Do** assign line colours by join order (red, blue, yellow, green, purple, ink) and keep a person's colour stable across screens.
**Do** outline yellow with a 1px ink inset wherever it is drawn as a line.
**Do** draw free as a solid line, busy as the ink hatch and unknown as the grey dashed track, in every view that shows availability.
**Do** mark the station as the confirmable slot with dashed guides, the ink time pill and a platform on every line free through it.
**Do** span the diagram over the useful day 08:00–24:00, the same track as the busy editor.
**Do** collapse beyond 6 people into the ink trunk with the "8/10" capsule, keeping at most 3 blocker lanes and a "Ver a todos" toggle.
**Do** keep every tap target at least 44px tall and one full-width primary action in a sticky footer.
**Do** write copy in Spanish (Chile), informal tú, through i18n keys.
donts: **Don't** use shadows or gradients for depth; the world is flat enamel.
**Don't** let colour carry state alone, and never draw an unanswered person as free.
**Don't** use line colours as decoration or behind body text where contrast fails.
**Don't** fall back to a days-by-people check table for availability.
**Don't** add a dark theme; light only is a decision, not a gap.
